Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:1.hebrew: וראשון עד אימת מיפטר - היכא דבא השני ונשתמש בו ולא כסהו, עד אימת רמיא כולה חיובא אשני וראשון פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:1.english: And until when is the first [one] exempt - Where the second [one] came and used it and did not cover it, until when does the entire liability fall upon the second [one] and the first [one] is exempt?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:2.hebrew: בכדי שידע - שיבא גם הראשון אחרי כן ויראנו מגולה. הואיל ושניהן יודעין שהוא מגולה, רמיא חיובא אתרוייהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:2.english: In the time it takes for him to know - [That is,] for the first one to also come afterward and see it uncovered. Since both of them know that it is uncovered, liability rests upon both of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:3.hebrew: ושמואל אמר בכדי שיודיעוהו - אע"פ שלא בא וראהו, חייב בחלקו, ולא רמיא כולה אשני, דהא לא גילהו דנחייביה משום פותח; לשון מורי. לשון אחר: עד כדי שיודיעוהו — אפי' בא וראהו, פטור עד שיודיעוהו. ולשון ראשון כשר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:3.english: And Shmuel said: Within the time that they inform him - Even though [the first person] did not come and see it, he is liable for his share, and the entire [liability] is not cast upon the second [person], since he did not uncover it that we should obligate him as one who opens [a pit]; [this is] the wording of my teacher. Another version: Until [the time] that they inform him — even if he came and saw it, he is exempt until they inform him. And the first version is sound.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:4.hebrew: ויכרות ארזים כו' - אבל לשני שבא ונשתמש בו, לא יהבינן שיעורא כולי האי, דהוה ליה לאותובי שומרים עילויה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:10:4.english: And cut cedars, etc. - However, to the second [person], who came and used it, we do not grant all this time, because he should have stationed guards over it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:12:1.english: And they weakened it - They damaged it and it became shaky.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:12:2.hebrew: ואתו שוורים ונפלו ביה - דאי נפלו ביה גמלים, לא מבעיא לן דחייב, דהא לגבי גמלים פושע הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:12:2.english: And oxen came and fell into it - For if camels fell into it, we have no dilemma that he is liable, since regarding camels he is negligent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:12:3.hebrew: אי שכיחי גמלים פושע הוא - אף לגבי שוורים, דאית ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה דגמלים מרעי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:12:3.english: If camels are [commonly] found, he is negligent - Even with respect to oxen, since he should have realized that camels would weaken it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:3:1.hebrew: משכוכית - לקמיה מפרש, דבר המושך כל העדר אחריו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:3:1.english: Mashkukhit - Further on, [the Gemara] explains [that it is] something that draws the entire flock after it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:4:1.hebrew: ה"ד אי במשיכה - שהכישה במקל ורצתה לפניו, שכן דרך בהמה דקה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:4:1.english: What are the circumstances? If by pulling - [meaning] that he struck it with a stick and it ran before him, for such is the way [of pulling] small livestock.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:4:2.english: Let him acquire [it] by pulling - Why do I need the handing over of [the] mashkukhit?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:4:3.hebrew: אי במסירה - קני להו, שהיה רה"ר או חצר שאינה של שניהן, שאין משיכה קונה שם, דאין משיכה אלא בסמטא או בחצר של שניהן, בהמוכר את הספינה בבבא בתרא (דף עו:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:4:3.english: If by conveying - [he] acquires them, [it is] because it was a public domain or a courtyard that does not belong to both of them, where pulling does not acquire, for pulling [acquires] only in an alleyway or in a courtyard belonging to both of them, [as stated] in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah in Bava Batra (76b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:1.hebrew: קרקשתא - גרסינן. זוג שמקרקש בה לפני העדר, והולך כולו אחריו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:1.english: Karkashta - This is our reading. [It is] a bell that [the shepherd] rings before the flock, and all of it goes after him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:2.hebrew: עיזא דאזלא בריש עדרא - יש לבעל העדר עז חריף, ודרך העזים להלך בראש, והעדר הולך אחריהם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:2.english: A goat that goes at the head of the flock - The owner of the flock has a spirited goat, and it is the way of goats to walk at the head [of the flock], and the flock walks after them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:3.hebrew: עביד לנגדא סמותא - לעז המושכת מנקר עיניה, ונכשלת ונופלת בבורות, והעדר אחריה. כך, כשהמקום נפרע משונאי ישראל, ממנה להן פרנסים שאינן מהוגנין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:5:3.english: He renders the leader blind - To the goat that leads [the flock], he gouges out its eyes, and it stumbles and falls into pits, and the flock [follows] after it. So too, when the Omnipresent exacts retribution from the enemies of Israel [i.e., Israel], He appoints for them leaders who are unworthy.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:1.english: The first one covered it - When he used it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:2.english: And the second came - To use it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:3.english: And found it uncovered - For example, where it became worm-eaten and the cover broke.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:4.hebrew: השני חייב - והראשון פטור, ובגמרא מפרש עד מתי ראשון פטור. אבל לא כסהו ראשון, ובא שני ומצאו מגולה ולא כסהו — שניהן חייבין. ודקתני השני חייב — הא אוקימנא שהניחו ראשון לשני משתמש, וסמך עליו שיכסנו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:4.english: The second is liable - And the first is exempt, and in the Gemara it explains until when the first is exempt. However, [if] the first did not cover it, and the second came and found it uncovered and did not cover it — both of them are liable. And [as for] that which [the Mishnah] taught, "the second is liable" — we have already established [that it refers to a case] where the first left the second using [it] and relied upon him to cover it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:5.english: [If] he covered it appropriately - And the ox or donkey passed over it and fell and died.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:6.hebrew: פטור - ובגמרא פריך, הואיל וכראוי הוא, היכי נפל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:6:6.english: Exempt - And in the Gemara it asks: since it was [covered] appropriately, how did [the animal] fall [in]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:1.hebrew: נפל לפניו מקול הכרייה - בור כרוייה, ונכנס כורה שכיר לתוכו להרחיב או להעמיק, ושור הולך על שפת הבור, ושמע קול הפטיש ונבעת, ונפל על פניו בבור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:1.english: [It] fell forward due to the sound of the digging - [There was] a dug pit, and a hired digger entered into it to widen or to deepen [it], and an ox was walking on the edge of the pit, and it heard the sound of the hammer and became frightened, and fell on its face into the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:2.hebrew: חייב - בעל הבור, ואפילו שור שהוא פקח — דאמר לקמן (בבא קמא דף נד:) במתניתא דבעל הבור פטור, דאיבעי עיוני ומיזל — הכא חייב, שקול הכרייה ביעתתו. ובגמרא פריך: נימא כורה גרם ליה. ל"א: לפניו מקול הכרייה, בעל הבור חייב; דאע"ג דאיכא למימר כורה גרם ליה, וכורה גרמא בעלמא הוא דעבד — דקי"ל: המבעית את חבירו פטור מדיני אדם — ותרוייהו ליפטרו, אפ"ה בעל הבור חייב כר' נתן, כדמפרש בגמ'. וזה שמעתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:2.english: Liable - [i.e.,] the owner of the pit [is liable]. And even [for] an ox that is sighted — as it says below (Bava Kamma 54b) in a baraita that the owner of the pit is exempt, because it should have looked as it walked — here he is liable, because the sound of the digging startled it. And in the Gemara it asks: Let us say the digger caused it! Another version: [If it fell] forward due to the sound of the digging, the owner of the pit is liable; for even though one could say the digger caused it, and the digger merely performed an indirect causation — as we hold [that] one who frightens his fellow is exempt under human laws — and [thus] both of them should be exempt, nevertheless the owner of the pit is liable in accordance with Rabbi Natan, as is explained in the Gemara. And this is what I heard.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:3.hebrew: לאחריו מקול הכרייה פטור - כדמפרש בגמרא. ואיידי דנקט ברישא מקול הכרייה, תנא סיפא לאחריו מקול הכרייה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:7:3.english: Backward due to the sound of the digging, [he is] exempt - As it explains in the Gemara. And since [the Mishnah] stated in the first clause "due to the sound of the digging," it taught [in] the latter clause "backward due to the sound of the digging."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:8:1.hebrew: בכלי שור - שייכא שבירה, העול והמחרישה. בכלי חמור שייכא קריעה, חבילת בגדים ומרדעת שעל גביו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:8:1.english: With the accoutrements of an ox - Breakage applies, [namely] the yoke and the plow. With the accoutrements of a donkey, tearing applies, [namely] a bundle of clothes and the packsaddle that is on its back.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:9:1.hebrew: שור חרש שוטה וקטן כו' - מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:9:1.english: An ox [that was] deaf, an imbecile, or young, etc. - [It] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:9:2.hebrew: בן או בת - כלומר, אע"ג דקטנים הן וליכא למימר איבעי להו עיוני ומיזל, אפ"ה פטור מגזירת הכתוב: "שור" ולא אדם, "חמור" ולא כלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 52a:9:2.english: A boy or a girl - That is to say, even though they are minors and one cannot say [that] they should have looked [carefully] as they walked, even so, [he] is exempt by scriptural decree: "an ox," and not a person; "a donkey," and not vessels.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:10:1.hebrew: בכדי שידע - כלומר, שהקול יצא שהבור מגולה, דמסתמא שמע. ושמואל אמר: בשמיעה בעלמא לא מחייב, דאין סומך אשמיעה, עד שיודיעוהו. ורבי יוחנן אמר: עד שיודיעוהו וישכור פועלים ויכרות ארזים. וה"ה השני, שנותנין לו שיעור זה, אלא דלא בעינן שיודיעוהו שכבר ידע. ושמואל סבר דמיד יש לו להושיב שם שומרים, שלא יפול שום דבר בבור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:10:1.english: [For the time] that he would know - That is to say, that word went out that the pit is uncovered, for presumably he heard [it]. And Shmuel said: through mere hearsay he is not liable, for one does not rely on hearsay, [so he is exempt] until they inform him. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: until they inform him, and he hires workers and cuts cedars [to cover it]. And the same applies to the second [person], that we grant him this [same] timeframe, except that we do not require that they inform him, since he already knows. And Shmuel holds that immediately [upon being informed] he must station guards there so that nothing falls into the pit:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:12:1.hebrew: ואתו שוורים ונפלו ביה - פ"ה דאי נפלו בו גמלים לא מיבעיא לן דחייב, דהא לגבי גמלים פושע הוא. וכן משמע הלשון. ויש ליתן טעם בדבר: דאפילו לא שכיחי גמלים כלל, יש לחוש שמא יבאו גמלים ויפלו, אבל אין לחוש שירעו גמלים ויפלו אחרי כן שוורים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:12:1.english: And oxen came and fell into it - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that if camels fell into it, we have no dilemma that he is liable, for with respect to camels he is negligent. And the wording [of the Gemara] implies this as well. And one can give a reason for this: that even if camels are not common at all, one must be concerned lest camels come and fall [into it], but one need not be concerned that camels will weaken [the cover] and oxen will fall [into it] afterward.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:1:1.hebrew: כיון דמסר לו מפתח קנה ה"ד [אי] בכספא כו' - רשב"ם מפרש בפ' חזקת הבתים (ב"ב ד' נב: ושם ד"ה נעל) גבי "נעל וגדר כל שהוא בנכסי הגר", ד"נעל" היינו שקבע מנעול בדלת לנעלו, דהוי בנין; אבל סגר הדלת בנכסי הגר — אין חזקה, דאין זה אלא כמבריח ארי מנכסי חבירו. ואע"ג דגבי שכירות הבתים אמר בריש מסכת פסחים (דף ד. ושם) דכשמסר לו מפתחות הוי בחזקת השוכר לבדוק, וה"ה לקנותו — ה"מ מוכר ומשכיר בית לחבירו; אבל בנכסי הגר, מאן מסר ליה דליקני? וקשה לר"י, דהכא משמע בהדיא דמסירת מפתח לא קני, אלא הוי כאומר "לך חזק וקני". ודוקא גבי חמץ הוא דתלוי במסירת מפתח, דמי שמפתח בידו עליו לבדוק, כיון שהוא יכול ליכנס בזה הבית לבדוק. ומה שפי' דלא קני בנעילת דלת — אין נראה. דבגיטין בפרק הזורק (גיטין דף עז:) אומר גבי גט: דתיזיל איהי ותיחוד ותפתח; אלמא נעילה לחוד קניא, שלא היה יכול לעשות שום מנעול, דשבת היה. ואע"פ שאסור לקנות בשבת, בשכיב מרע שרי, שלא תטרוף דעתו, כדאמרי' בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קנו: ושם). ובחזקת הבתים (שם דף נז.) נמי מוכח, גבי ההוא דתנן: "אלו דברים שיש להם חזקה ואלו שאין להם חזקה". ופריך הגמרא: "מ"ש רישא ומ"ש סיפא?" ומשני, אמר רבא: "כל שאילו בנכסי הגר קנה — בנכסי חבירו קנה; בנכסי הגר לא קנה — בנכסי חבירו לא קנה". א"כ, הא דקתני סיפא: "הכניס תרנגולין לתוך הבית, הרי זו חזקה" — בנכסי הגר נמי קנה! והיינו טעמא דקנה, דמסתמא כשנתן שם תרנגולין נעל דלת כדי לשמרם; אלמא בנעילת דלת סגי. ואין לדמות נעילת דלת למבריח ארי, דדוקא "נתן צרור דסכר מיניה מיא" הוא דאמרי' בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נג.) דהוי כמבריח ארי; אבל נעל, שנעל דלת בפני כל אדם ואין מניח אדם ליכנס, מוכחא מילתא שהבית שלו וקני בנעילה לחודה. והא דאמר התם: "הבונה פלטרין בנכסי הגר, ובא אחר והעמיד להם דלתות — קנה", אורחא דמילתא נקט, שאותו שמעמיד דלתות רגיל לנעלם, וה"ה נעל ולא העמיד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 52a:1:1.english: Once he has conveyed the key to him, he has acquired [it]; what are the circumstances? [If] by money, etc. - Rashbam explains in the chapter [entitled] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 52b, and there s.v. na'al) regarding [the ruling] "locked or fenced any amount in the property of a convert [who died without heirs]," that "locked" means he affixed a lock to the door in order to lock it, which is [an act of] building; however, if he merely closed the door in the property of a convert, it is not [an act of] taking possession (chazakah), for this is nothing more than chasing a lion away from another's property. And even though regarding the rental of houses [the Gemara] says at the beginning of tractate Pesachim (4a and there [in the commentaries]) that when he handed over the keys to him, it is in the possession of the tenant to search [for chametz], and the same applies to acquiring it — that applies only where one sells or rents a house to another, but in the property of a convert, who handed [the key] over to him that he should acquire [it]? However, Ri finds this difficult, for here it is clearly implied that handing over a key does not effect acquisition [by itself], rather it is merely like saying, "Go, take possession, and acquire [it]." And it is specifically regarding chametz that [the obligation] depends on handing over the key, because whoever has the key in his hand is obligated to search, since he is able to enter this house to search. And what [Rashbam] explained, that one does not acquire by locking the door [alone], does not seem [correct]. For in Gittin, in the chapter [entitled] HaZorek (Gittin 77b), [the Gemara] says regarding a bill of divorce: "let her go, close [the door], and open [it]," which proves that locking alone effects acquisition — since he could not have made any lock, as it was Shabbat. And even though it is forbidden to acquire on Shabbat, in the case of a critically ill person (shechiv mera) it is permitted so that his mind not become distraught, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMeit (Bava Batra 156b and there [in the commentaries]). And in Chezkas HaBatim (ibid., 57a) it is also proven, regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: "These are the things that have chazakah, and these are the things that do not have chazakah." And the Gemara asks: "What is the difference between the first clause and the latter clause?" And Rava answers: "Anything that if [done] in the property of a convert he acquires, in the property of another he acquires; [and anything that] in the property of a convert he does not acquire, in the property of another he does not acquire." If so, that which the latter clause teaches: "[If] he brought chickens into the house, this is a chazakah" — in the property of a convert he also acquires! And the reason he acquires is that presumably when he put chickens there, he locked the door in order to guard them — which proves that locking the door suffices. And one should not compare locking a door to chasing away a lion, for it is specifically [the case of] "one who placed a pebble and dammed water away from it" that we say in Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 53a) is like chasing away a lion; whereas [when] he locked — meaning he locked the door before everyone and does not allow anyone to enter — it is evident that the house is his, and he acquires by locking alone. And as for that which [the Gemara] says there: "One who builds a mansion in the property of a convert, and another comes and sets up doors for it, acquires [it]" — it speaks of the usual case, for the one who sets up doors is accustomed to locking them, and the same applies if he locked [existing doors] without setting [them] up:
